Prachchhak Sd/- ================================================================ Approved for Reporting Yes x ================================================================ Girish Bhogilal Vohra Versus Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani & Anr. ================================== = = = = = = Appearance: Ms. Shaili A Kapadia(3453) for the Appellant(s) No. 1 Ms Megha Chitalia App for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 2 Rule Served for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1 ======== == == == = = == Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Hemant M. Prachchhak Date : 13/12/2024 Oral Judgment
texts.facts: 2. It is the case of the appellant that the on 31/07/2006 at 02.00 p.m., the appellant - Food Inspector accompanied by peon, Jayantilal Solanki visited Jai Mithu Products, 155, Kotarpur, Nobelnagar, Ahmedabad wherein the respondent No.1 was present and doing the business. One gentleman passing through the area Dayalbhai Vanjumal Jaswani was called as a Panch Witness and in his presence the appellant has disclosed his identity and inquired about the food articles. 2.1 In presence of the panch, the respondent accused informed that the said food article is Cornflour (BBC Brand) and the price of one kg. plastic bag is Rs.20/-. The appellant paid Rs.60/- in cash in presence of panch and purchased three bags of Cornflour (BBC Brand) each of one kilogram. After following the due procedure under the law and after giving the intimation to the accused person in his presence and in the presence of Panch Witness, the sample was collected and necessary Panchnama is made. 2.3 The sample was sent to the Laboratory for the purpose of public analysis. The report of the Public Analyst reveals that though the ingredients disclosed in the plastic bag reveals that it contains the permitted synthetic colour, however, the same was not found in the sample and thus, the sample was clearly misbranded. Therefore, after following the due procedure and after receiving the sanction, the complaint was registered against the accused person. 2.4 The charge is framed against the Accused person, wherein the Accused pleaded as not guilty and proceeded to face the trial. The prosecution has led oral as well as documentary evidence to bring home the charges. The further statement of the Accused is recorded under Section 313 of the Code. 3. Being aggrieved and feeling dissatisfied with the impugned order passed by the trial Court acquitting the present respondent accused, the appellant has preferred present appeal.
texts.arguments: Ms. Shaili Kapadia, learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that the trial Court has completely overlooked the evidence led by the appellant and thereby the trial Court committed serious error of law and on facts both. She has further submitted that the evidence led by the prosecution including the oral as well as the documentary more particularly, the analysis report clearly mentioned that the sample was substandard and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined adulterated and therefore, the case for mis-branding and adulteration was lodged against present respondent accused however, without considering and appreciating the same the trial Court has passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal in favour of respondent accused, which is erroneous, illegal and unjust. 5.1 Learned Counsel for the Girish Bhogilal Vohra vs Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471337/ 2 appellant has further contended that the public analyst report established the guilt of the present respondent accused, however the same was not properly appreciated by the trial Court while passing the impugned judgment and order of acquittal. 5.2 Learned Counsel for the appellant has further submitted that the complainant Food Inspector, through his deposition, has established that he is competent to file the prosecution against the present respondent accused and having a valid authorization and also the sanctioned given by the Deputy Commissioner is in consonance with the settled legal principle, however NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined said fact was not properly considered by the trial Court, in its true and proper spirit. 5.3 Learned Counsel for the appellant has further submitted that so far as the manner and method in which the sample was collected and sent, all the statutory procedure under the Act was followed and the sample was sent for the public analyst however, all these facts were not properly appreciated by the trial Court in its true and proper spirit, while passing the impugned judgment and order of acquittal. 5.4 In view of the above submissions, learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned judgment and order of trial Court is not in consonance with the settled legal principle and the same may be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK] and present appeal filed against the acquittal of the respondents accused may be allowed. 11. At this stage, it is appropriate to take into account the decision in case of Gangadhar Yashvant Ramekar vs. Mukeshbhai B. Shah and others reported in 1999(2) GCD 1292 in paragraph No.12 has held as under:- NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined "12. In the said decision, it was observed that the person who cleaned the bottles was not examined and there was satisfactory evidence to show that the mandatory requirements were not complied with and, therefore, the benefit was given to the accused persons relying upon the decision of this High Court in the case of M.B. Risaldar v. Radheshyam as reported in 1980(2) GLR 136. The facts of the present case are identical as can be seen from the deposition of the complainant" Girish Bhogilal Vohra vs Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471337/ 4 12. The Hon'ble Apex Court has in a series of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined judgments enunciated the principles while exercising jurisdiction under Section 378 against acquittal, the power of the Appellate Court is inasmuch as re- appreciate the evidence, view or re-consider the evidence and if the Court finds that there is any illegality or any irregularity in the judgment then in that case only, the Court has power to entertain the appeal and interfere with the order of acquittal. The scope and principles are enunciated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Chandrappa and others Vs. State of Karnataka reported in (2007) 4 SCC 415, more particularly paragraphs 42 and 43, which was subsequently re- affirmed by the Hon'ble Apex Court Rajesh Prasad Vs. State of Bihar and another, reported in [2022] 3 SCC 471, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has enunciated the general principles in case of acquittal, more particularly in paragraph 26 the general principles are set out by the Hon'ble Apex Court based upon various decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court. Then in case of Babu Sahebagouda Rudragoudar Vs. State of Karnataka, reported in NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined AIR 2024 SC 2252 = (2024) 8 SCC 149, the Hon'ble Apex Court has dealt with the similar issue, more particularly, in paragraph Nos. 37 to 40. Hence, I am in complete agreement with the findings recorded by the trial Court. 15. It is also worthwhile to refer to the recent decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramesh vs. State of Karnataka, reported in [2024] 9 SCC 169, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held and observed in paras-20 and 21 as under:- "20. At this stage, it would be relevant to refer to the general principles culled out by this Court in Chandrappa and others vs. State of Karnataka , regarding the power of Girish Bhogilal Vohra vs Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471337/ 5 the appellate Court while dealing with an appeal against a judgment of acquittal. The principles read thus: "42. .... (1) An appellate court has full power to review, reappreciate and reconsider the evidence upon which the order of acquittal is founded. (2) The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 puts no limitation, restriction or condition on exercise of such power and an appellate court on the evidence before it may reach its own conclusion, both on questions of fact and of law. Such phraseologies are more in the nature of "flourishes of language" to emphasize the reluctance of an appellate court to interfere with acquittal than to curtail the power of the court to review the evidence and to come to its own conclusion. Firstly, the presumption of innocence is available to him under the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that every person shall be presumed to be innocent unless he is proved guilty by a competent court of law. Secondly, the accused having secured his acquittal, the presumption of his innocence is further reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened by the trial court. 21. In Rajendra Prasad v. State of Bihar, a three-Judge Bench of this Court pointed out that it would be essential for the High Court, in an appeal against acquittal, to clearly indicate firm and weighty grounds from the record for discarding the reasons of the Trial Court in order to be able to reach a contrary conclusion of guilt of the accused.
